supporting_observations.claim: At 13:41:56 UTC, PowerShell running as maria.lopez executed Compress-Archive against \\FILE-HD-01\Shared\Clients, targeting C:\Users\maria.lopez\AppData\Local\Temp\c.zip. A file-creation event confirms creation of that archive path.
At 13:45:24 UTC, Explorer launched Chrome PID 4896 as maria.lopez with https://sendbox-files.io/ as its command-line destination, in the same logon session used for archive creation.

At approximately 13:48:17 UTC, the proxy recorded an authenticated maria.lopez tunnel to sendbox-files.io:443 carrying 51,000,000 client-to-server bytes and 8,800 server-to-client bytes. Zeek independently recorded approximately 51 MB outbound on the workstation-to-proxy connection.
Endpoint network events attribute that large-transfer connection, using source port 65454 and proxy destination 10.30.20.30:8080, to Chrome PID 4896 running as maria.lopez.

The sequence of client-share archiving followed by a directly correlated 51 MB outbound browser transfer to sendbox-files.io supports suspected data exfiltration and a malicious disposition. The supplied inventory does not approve this service. This finding rests on the alerted transfer and its preceding staging activity, not unrelated anomalies.

known_telemetry_limitations: The sendbox connection is logged as a CONNECT tunnel, without an inspected HTTP request body or uploaded filename; its contents cannot be identified from these records (T019-00171).

The matching large-transfer records are timestamped approximately 13:48:17 UTC, rather than the alert's approximate 13:46 UTC time. Confirm the original alert's flow identifiers and timestamp semantics (T019-00170 through T019-00173).

The supplied collection-status metadata reports missing WS-LPARK-01 endpoint logs from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC. This does not remove the direct workstation, proxy, and network evidence supporting this assessment.
claims_not_established: That c.zip was the object transmitted, or that the transmitted data contained client or patient information; the archive creation and outbound tunnel are established separately (T019-00119, T019-00171).
That the archive completed successfully with all intended source files; file creation alone does not establish archive completeness (T019-00117, T019-00119).

Whether Maria personally initiated the activity, whether her session was compromised, or what the operator's intent was; execution and proxy authentication identify an account, not a physical actor (T019-00117, T019-00150, T019-00171).
That the remote application accepted and retained a complete uploaded file; CONNECT status 200 and byte counts do not establish application-level upload completion (T019-00171).
additional_evidence_needed: Retrieve the original alert flow details to reconcile its approximate 13:46 UTC timestamp with T019-00170 through T019-00173.
Preserve c.zip, inspect its contents and size, and obtain relevant file-share access records to establish the staged dataset (T019-00117, T019-00119).
Preserve Chrome history, upload artifacts, and any available DLP or destination-side transaction records to identify the transmitted object and recipient (T019-00150, T019-00171).
Validate business purpose and authorization with the user and data owner while preserving the endpoint evidence associated with the archive and transfer (T019-00117, T019-00171).
unrelated_findings: Separately investigate two quiet executions of dotnet-sdk-installer.exe from the user's Temp directory after the transfer. These records do not establish malware or a connection to the alerted activity (T019-00181, T019-00210).

Separately review Tableau Online usage against the supplied service-approval inventory. Later browser requests include bootstrap, JavaScript, favicon, and render-tooltip operations; these are not the alerted sendbox transfer (T019-00257, T019-00258, T019-00264, T019-00268, T019-00272).
